adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a clear stored-XSS path for imported content. In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (which is where Discourse typically sanitizes/filters HTML). In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, feed items are ingested via `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then passed into `TopicEmbed.import(...)` without any sanitization; `CGI.unescapeHTML` can convert escaped entities like `<script>` back into executable `<script>` tags. In app/models/topic_embed.rb, those contents are saved into a Post with `cook_method: :raw_html`, ensuring the bypass applies. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — `rss.items.each` is unbounded — no cap, no date cutoff, no cursor. A 10k-entry feed creates 10k topics with all their post-create side effects in one hourly job

On a large feed (e.g., thousands of items), the hourly scheduled job will process every entry in a single run, and on first run (or if many URLs are new) it can create a large number of topics/posts and trigger associated side effects. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:28 — Revise path passes `bypass_rate_limiter` but not `bypass_bump`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `contents << "…"` mutates the caller's string argument in place — corruption for any caller that reuses the buffer, `FrozenError` for a frozen literal. `contents + "…"` costs nothing

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the line `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends to the `contents` string in place. This is a real side-effect introduced by the diff: any caller that reuses the same `contents` object after calling `import` will see it modified, and if a caller ever passes a frozen string, this will raise `FrozenError`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:16,37 — `content_sha1` is computed over content that *includes* the localized `embed.imported_from` footer — changing site locale or that translation string re-digests every imported article, mass-revising the entire corpus

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the method mutates `contents` by appending a localized footer string via `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)` before computing `content_sha1` (`content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)`). On subsequent imports for the same `embed_url`, the code compares the newly computed SHA1 to the stored one and revises the post if it differs. Therefore, changing the translation string for `embed.imported_from` (or changing the locale used during import) will change the computed SHA1 even if the upstream article content is unchanged, causing unnecessary revisions/updates across all imported posts when feeds are polled or retrieved again.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:130 — The `raw_html` early return also skips `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, …)` and silently ignores the `cooking_options` contract. Every plugin hooked on that filter is bypassed for imported posts with no way for the author to know

Therefore, any plugins relying on the `:after_post_cook` filter will not run for `raw_html` posts (e.g., those created by `TopicEmbed.import` with `cook_method: :raw_html`), and any arguments/options passed to `cook` are ignored in that case. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` applies to the `loading` render too, so a successfully-imported topic stays behind a stale placeholder for up to a minute; it also caches a `current_user`-dependent `TopicView` (unverifiable — `application_controller.rb` absent)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid directive (spec allows `DENY`/`SAMEORIGIN`/`ALLOW-FROM`). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16 — `post.user.small_avatar_url` / `.username` with no nil guard; `posts.user_id` is nullable, so one deleted author 500s the entire embed inside the customer's iframe

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:8 — `embed_url` isn't coerced to String — `?embed_url[]=x` and `?embed_url[a]=b` both satisfy `params.require`, then raise `TypeError`/`ArgumentError` in `URI()`, which only rescues `URI::InvalidURIError`. That value is then passed to `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` which calls `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url)`: with a hash/Parameters this can raise (e.g., quoting error) causing an unhandled 500. If no topic is found, the controller enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` with the same unvalidated `embed_url`; the job calls `TopicRetriever.new(args[:embed_url])`, and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` calls `URI(@embed_url)` but only rescues `URI::InvalidURIError`—passing an Array/Hash will raise `TypeError` (not rescued), causing job failures. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:10 — `raise Discourse::InvalidParameters` for a permanent, non-transient condition asks the queue to retry — if `Jobs::Base` leaves Sidekiq's default policy in place, each malformed enqueue burns 25 slots over ~21 days. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:59 — Port test `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` is scheme-blind — `https://host:80` and `http://host:443` both lose their port. Should be `uri.port != uri.default_port`

This incorrectly drops an explicitly specified non-default port when it happens to be 80 on an `https://` URL or 443 on an `http://` URL (e.g., `https://example.com:80/...` would produce a prefix without `:80`). The correct check should be scheme-aware (e.g., `uri.port != uri.default_port`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:14 — Per-post `post.user` and `post.url` (which dereferences `post.topic`) in the render loop — up to 2 extra queries per post if `TopicView` doesn't preload. Bounded at 5 by `{best: 5}`; `lib/topic_view.rb` absent so unverified

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:20 — Resize protocol is one-shot and one-directional: measured once in `window.onload`, no re-measure on reflow (late images, web fonts, CSS FOUC), no host→frame channel. With `scrolling="no"`, any post-load growth is clipped permanently

adjudication.rationale: The diff implements iframe auto-resizing by sending a single `postMessage` from the embedded page only once in `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` via `window.onload` (posting `{type:'discourse-resize', height: document['body'].offsetHeight}`). On the host side (`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`) the iframe has `scrolling="no"` and only updates height when it receives such messages, but no further messages are ever sent after onload. Therefore any later layout height changes (e.g., parent width changes causing reflow, late-loading webfonts, or other post-load reflow) will not be reflected and can lead to clipped content. The finding’s file/line reference is off (it’s not in `best.html.erb`), but the underlying one-shot/one-direction resize issue is real in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:21 — `iframe.height = height + "px"` — the HTML `height` *attribute* takes a bare number, not a CSS length. Should be `iframe.style.height`

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the resize handler sets `iframe.height = e.data.height + "px";`. The `height` IDL attribute reflects the HTML `height` attribute on `<iframe>`, which is defined as a non-negative integer (CSS pixels) and is typically set as a bare number (e.g. `300`), not a CSS length with units. Appending `"px"` can lead to an invalid attribute value and potentially prevent resizing in some user agents; the robust fix is either `iframe.height = e.data.height` (no units) or `iframe.style.height = e.data.height + "px"`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4 — DB-level `NOT NULL` on `topic_id`/`post_id` with no matching model validations (only `embed_url` and `content_sha1` are validated) — failures surface as raw `PG::NotNullViolation` instead of `RecordInvalid`. adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85` vs `lib/post_creator.rb:79 — `skip_validations` now means different things in sibling APIs — in `PostCreator` it also suppresses `SpamRulesEnforcer`; in `PostRevisor` only AR validations. `Post#revise` forwards `opts` verbatim, widening reach.
